title: Canadian Whisky
subtitle: Canadian whisky and the American market
description: How Canadian whisky is made, grain by grain, and how distillers in Ontario and Quebec came to supply the United States. Four pours.

pours.name: Canadian Club 1858
pours.notes: Walker’s brand, still made in Walkerville. Smell it before you add anything, then try it with a splash of soda or water.

pours.name: Lot No. 40
pours.origin: Corby, at the Hiram Walker distillery, Windsor
pours.notes: All rye, from a single copper pot still. This is close to what a flavouring whisky tastes like before it is blended.

pours.name: Crown Royal Fine Deluxe
pours.notes: Seagram’s blend from 1939, now made by Diageo. Compare it with the Canadian Club: two big blends, built mostly on base whisky.

pours.name: Forty Creek Copper Pot Reserve
pours.notes: A winemaker’s whisky from the Niagara Peninsula. The grains are distilled and aged apart, then blended.
